Description: The ‘Year Ahead Constraint Limits’ dataset (https://www.neso.energy/data-portal/year-ahead-constraint-limits) is superseded by the ‘24 Month Ahead Constraint Limits’ dataset and has not been updated for over 3 years. For the avoidance of confusion, ‘Year Ahead Constraint Limits’ dataset will be removed from the Data Portal on 24th July 2026.

Due to the technical issues, we have been experiencing some difficulties in using the Datastore APIs and download requests. We have corrected the issue now and these services are working as expected. We apologise for the inconvenience caused during this period.

We are currently experiencing issues with the quality of the published SOP data in the Data Portal. Our team is actively investigating the matter and working towards a resolution. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused by technical issues with the Data Portal Subscription. Unexpected emails are being sent to subscribers about new datasets being added and datasets being deleted, as well as some data files being missed on Data Portal. Our IT team has been notified of the issue and is working on a solution. We have neither added nor deleted any datasets or data files and all the data can still be accessed via APIs. We appreciate your patience as we work to resolve this issue as quickly as possible.
Notes: The issue is resolved now. We can see all the datasets and data files, all the data portal functionalities are now working as expected. Apologies for the inconvenience caused.

Description: We are pleased to confirm that the fix for the ???_id??? column into csv files bug has been deployed and from now on any downloaded csv files will not show the column "_id".

We have noticed that for some of our datasets there is a issues with the metadata ???last_modified??? update field. The new metadata "metadata_modified" has been created to provide the last updated timestamp for all datasets. Please be aware that if a dataset is not updated, the old metadata ???last_modified??? will still show the last updated timestamp.
